# prefer version tag when multiple tags available

When a commit carries several tags, `git release` should pick the version-like one:

```
commit 3942eb0c9abc450a6a4eccc7cdacd00b853d1c66 (HEAD -> extended, tag: v0.1.2, tag: goimports, origin/extended, origin/HEAD, mirror/extended)
```

Here `git describe --tags` may return `goimports` (a marker tag on the go-tools fork, [[DOT-165]]) instead of `v0.1.2`; the release command should filter out non-numeric tags and, among the remaining ones, choose deterministically.

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/169#issuecomment-5711684205
See the note in #60: the "prefer numeric tag" filter works for the example by coincidence (`goimports` contains `p`), not by design. Also `sort -V | head -1` picks the lowest version if a commit carries two different ones.
-->
